channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Euro tumbles as Japanese Yen benefits from BoJ rate hike bets
item.description: EUR/JPY falls 1.11% on Monday and trades around 179.45 at the time of writing. The sharp decline in the cross mainly reflects the strong appreciation of the Japanese Yen (JPY), supported by growing expectations of monetary policy tightening by the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: EM FX: Policy holds shape CLP, PLN, PEN, TRY – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects Chile, Poland, Peru and Türkiye to keep policy rates unchanged at upcoming meetings.

item.title: Czech Koruna: CPI keeps CNB on hold but risks build – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose notes that Czech August CPI matched expectations and CNB forecasts, keeping inflation within target and allowing rates to stay unchanged on 17 September.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $65.90 per troy ounce, down 0.47% from the $66.21 it cost on Friday.

item.title: ECB: Political strains test policy shield – Rabobank
item.description: RaboResearch notes that the ECB’s Transmission Protection Instrument provides a backstop for Eurozone government bonds during stress not justified by fundamentals.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Inflation data steer policy path – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir expect August Consumer Price Index (CPI) to prove subdued enough to keep the Federal Reserve (Fed) on hold in September, with the CPI-to-PCE translation also pointing to contained underlying inflation.

item.title: UK Chancellor Healey: I will build on Reeves' move to recover fiscal discipline
item.description: United Kingdom (UK) Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey signaled in a scheduled speech during the European trading session on Monday that the government will continue focusing on maintaining fiscal discipline, in an attempt to contain higher borrowing costs.

item.title: Brent: Supply risks support prices – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Bank’s Danske Research Team notes Brent crude trading near USD 97 as renewed US-Iran strikes around the Strait of Hormuz raise concerns over prolonged disruptions to Middle East energy flows.

item.title: Indian Rupee remains higher as FX inflows optimism keeps outweiging oil strain
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week.

item.title: Dow Jones futures fall as inflationary risks rise
item.description: Dow Jones futures are down by 0.32% to trade near 53,270 during European hours on Monday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures steady near 7,720, while Nasdaq 100 futures advance by 0.31% to trade around 29,660. The US stock market will be closed Monday for the Labor Day holiday.

item.title: WTI struggles to hold above $90 despite material supply risks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, turns upside down to near $89.50 during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: British Pound dives to six-month low vs rallying Yen amid bets for faster BoJ rate hikes
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross meets with heavy supply during the early part of the European session on Monday and weakens below the 209.00 mark, hitting its lowest level since February 24 amid a broad-based rally in the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: US Dollar: Inflation data guide blackout repricing – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that strong U.S. payrolls have lifted September Fed hike odds back toward 60%, leaving rate expectations highly data-dependent as the Fed enters its blackout.

item.title: Euro: Tight range with downside bias against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner argues that Euro fundamentals remain contained despite German regional election results highlighting political tensions for Chancellor Merz’s CDU. Solid Eurozone growth and investor confidence are offset by downside risks from this week’s ECB meeting.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Downside risks build against Yen as policy diverges – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research strategist Philip Wee highlights growing downside risks in CHF/JPY after the cross failed to re-enter its February–July 198–204 range and slipped to 193.

item.title: Euro remains stronger against Canadian Dollar following Eurozone Investor Confidence
item.description: EUR/CAD remains stronger for the second consecutive day, trading around 1.6080 during European hours on Monday.

item.title: Gold recovers intraday losses to sub-$4,400 as USD slumps despite Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) shows some resilience below the $4,400 mark and recovers intraday losses during the first half of the European session on Monday. Any meaningful upside, however, seems limited as traders might opt to wait on the sidelines ahead of the latest US inflation figures, due later this week.

item.title: Eurozone Sentix Investor Confidence improves significantly to 5.1 in September
item.description: Eurozone’s Sentix Investor Confidence data, a key indicator of Investor morale, comes in significantly higher at 5.1 in September from 0.9 in August. The sentiment data turned positive in August after remaining negative in the previous five months.

item.title: Swiss Franc ticks up against US Dollar following Swiss employment data
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) bounced up against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday.

item.title: Euro: Limited gains from ECB tightening – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen argues that EUR/USD remains primarily driven by the US Dollar, with Euro-side developments only amplifying or dampening trends.

item.title: British Pound edges higher against US Dollar, UK Chancellor Healey’s speech eyed
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is marginally higher at around 1.3525 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: British Pound: BoE repricing risk weighs on Sterling – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad argues that United Kingdom (UK) July Gross Domestic Product (GDP), expected flat month-on-month, is unlikely to alter Bank of England (BoE) expectations.

item.title: Forex Today: Middle East tensions keep investors on edge
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Monday, September 7:

item.title: New Zealand Dollar struggles due to cautious RBNZ policy outlook
item.description: NZD/USD depreciates after two days of gains, trading around 0.5880 during European hours on Monday. The pair depreciates as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) faces pressure from cautious sentiment surrounding the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s (RBNZ) policy outlook.

item.title: US Dollar: Strong payrolls fail to sustain Dollar gains – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan notes the Dollar strengthened after a stronger-than-expected August US jobs report, with Nonfarm Payrolls and labour participation surprising to the upside while wage growth eased.

item.title: Canadian Dollar consolidates below mid-1.3800s as oil strength offsets USD Fed support
item.description: The USD/CAD pair extends its sideways consolidative price move through the early European session on Monday and currently trades just below mid-1.3800s.

item.title: Oil: Prices climb on supply risks – UOB
item.description: According to UOB strategists Oil prices extended gains, with Brent crude settling above $96 and posting a strong weekly rise as disruptions to Middle East supply routes and renewed geopolitical tensions supported energy markets.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD dips below $66.00 and hints at a bearish “H&S”
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) nudges lower on Monday, hitting session lows in the mid-$65.00s after a reversal from the $68.00 area.

item.title: Euro: Support at 180 eyed against Yen on BoJ risk – DBS
item.description: DBS strategist Philip Wee argues that downside risk in EUR/JPY is less straightforward than in CHF/JPY.

item.title: Equities: Labour data weighs on stocks – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research notes that a strong US labour market report increased expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve, pressuring global equities. The S&P 500 declined while the Stoxx 600 posted a small gain, with cyclicals outperforming and rate-sensitive sectors underperforming.
